name: Asriel
title: Founder of a clan in the tribe of Manasseh
summary: Asriel was a prominent figure within the tribe of Manasseh and became the ancestor of the clan of the Asrielites, one of the most important family groups in this tribe. His genealogical placement varies between biblical sources: In Numbers he appears as the son of Gilead and thus the great-grandson of Manasseh, while 1 Chronicles places him in a different genealogical context where an Aramaic concubine is mentioned – although there is textual uncertainty regarding this verse. The various traditions illuminate the complex origins of the tribe of Manasseh and its contact with surrounding peoples. During the allocation of land in Canaan under Joshua's leadership, the clan of the Asrielites received their share of the inheritance west of the Jordan, in the central highlands that later became the core area of Samaria.

keyEvents.title: Registered as Gilead's son
keyEvents.description: Asriel is listed as one of the sons of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Manasseh, in the census in Numbers. Through him, the clan of the Asrielites was established as an independent family group within the tribe of Manasseh.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: In 1 Chronicles, Asriel appears in the genealogy of Manasseh in a context where an Aramean concubine is mentioned. There is textual uncertainty regarding who this concubine was the mother of, but tradition offers a supplementary and partially divergent picture of his genealogy compared to Numbers.

keyEvents.title: The land allocation for the tribe of Manasseh
keyEvents.description: As part of the tribe of Manasseh, Asriel's clan received its share of the inheritance west of the Jordan during the land distribution led by Joshua. The Asrielites are explicitly mentioned among the clans that received territories in the central highlands.

versions.summary: Asriel was a descendant of Manasseh, son of Joseph, and founder of the clan of the Asrielites. He is mentioned in connection with the land distribution in Canaan, where his clan received its share of the inheritance. He is one of the recorded family heads within the tribe of Manasseh.
versions.title: Descendant of Manasseh
versions.reason: [minor] The title 'Descendant of Manasseh' is correct but could be more descriptive. 'Founder of a clan in the tribe of Manasseh' would better reflect his role.; [minor] The role 'leader' is somewhat vague. Asriel is primarily known as a clan founder or family head rather than a general 'leader'. 'Clan founder' and 'family head' would be more precise.; [minor] The title 'Mentioned in the genealogy of Manasseh' is a bit passive. A more active phrasing could be 'Recorded as Gilead's son'.; [minor] Verse 32 in Numbers 26 concerns Zelophehad's daughters and other information, not directly about the establishment of Asriel's clan. Only verse 31 is sufficient to refer to the Asrielites.; [minor] The list of siblings matches Numbers 26:30–32 (Gilead's sons), but it should be noted that Hefer in verse 32 is listed separately, and Zelophehad (Hefer's son) is also mentioned in context. The list is acceptable as it stands.; [minor] In 1 Chronicles 7:14 the genealogy differs somewhat from Numbers—here Asriel is mentioned as a son born to his Aramean concubine. This is an interesting detail that should be reflected in the description.; [major] The profile lacks footnotes. There are several interesting linguistic and theological details about Asriel that should be included, such as the meaning of his name and the genealogical difference between Numbers and 1 Chronicles.

versions.summary: Asriel was a descendant of Manasseh, son of Joseph, and founder of the clan of the Asrielites. In Numbers he is listed as the son of Gilead, son of Makir, while 1 Chronicles mentions him as the son of Manasseh's Aramean concubine. His clan was one of the recognized clans within the tribe of Manasseh that received its share of the inheritance in Canaan west of the Jordan during the land distribution led by Joshua.

It may be considered to set a more descriptive value, but since we do not have an ID for her, null is acceptable.; [minor] The summary closely resembles the previous version (version 1). versions.summary: Asriel belonged to the tribe of Manasseh and became the ancestor of the clan of the Asrielites, one of the recognized family groups within this tribe. He appears in two different genealogical traditions: according to one, he was the son of Gilead and thus a great-grandson of Manasseh, while the other tradition links him directly to Manasseh through an Aramaic wife. These parallel traditions testify to the mixed origins of the tribe of Manasseh and its connections with surrounding peoples. During the allocation of land in Canaan, led by Joshua, Asriel's clan received their inheritance west of the Jordan, in the central highlands that later became known as the Samaria region.
versions.title: Founder of a clan in the tribe of Manasseh
versions.reason: [minor] According to Num 26:30-32, Asriel's "brothers" (i.e., parallel clans under Gilead) are Iezer (Abiezer), Helek, Shechem, Shemida, and Hepher. Iezer/Abiezer is missing from the list. Although he is sometimes called Abiezer, he should be included for completeness.; [minor] 1 Chr 7:14 is a difficult verse text-critically. The phrasing "his mother was Manasseh's Aramean concubine" is one reading, but many scholars interpret the verse to mean that it was Makir's mother (not Asriel's) who was the Aramean concubine. This should be nuanced somewhat to reflect this uncertainty.; [minor] The summary is good, but to distinguish itself clearly from earlier versions and to be even more precise, it could nuance the interpretation of 1 Chr 7:14, where there is text-critical uncertainty about whose mother the Aramean concubine was.

footnotes.text: The name Asriel (Hebrew: אַשְׂרִיאֵל, 'Asri'el') likely means 'God's promise' or 'God has made happy', composed of the Hebrew verb 'ashar' (to be happy/blessed) and 'El' (God). Some scholars interpret the name as 'promise from God' (from 'esher' – happiness/blessing).

There is a remarkable difference in the genealogy: In Numbers 26:31, Asriel is listed as the son of Gilead, while in 1 Chronicles 7:14, Asriel appears in a different genealogical context. The text in 1 Chron 7:14 is however text-critically difficult, and there is disagreement over whom the Aramaic wife was the mother of – Asriel or Machir. The difference can be explained by the fact that Numbers gives a simplified clan structure where 'son' is used in the sense of 'descendant', while Chronicles preserves an older or alternative genealogical tradition.

The clan of the Asrielites is one of the clans in the Gilead branch of the tribe of Manasseh that was allotted land west of the Jordan (Joshua 17:2). Archaeological findings in the central highlands of Samaria confirm settlement in this area during the late Bronze Age and early Iron Age, which aligns with the biblical account of the land distribution.

The connections to Aramean peoples reflected in Manasseh's genealogy reflect the complex ethnic composition of the northern Israelite tribes. Such cultural and familial ties between Israelites and Arameans are well attested in the biblical texts and correspond with what we know about population conditions in the region during the late Bronze Age.

The Samaria ostraca, clay inscriptions from the 700s BC found in the Israelite capital of Samaria, mention the clan names of Manasseh's descendants – including a reference that may be linked to Asriel's clan. This is a rare example of extra-biblical sources confirming biblical clan structures.
